title: Clave versus the four-beat jazz bar
summary: He explains clave spans two bars, the downbeat is felt not played.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Uh-huh. I'm interested in the -- can you talk a little more, because these are things that people who are coming from the jazz side don't understand about the differences between jazz rhythm as it was with the basic four to

Well, let me tell you one thing. The bar got four beats. The CLAVE is a combination of two bars, one, two, three, one, two, three, two bars. Like I told Dizzy one time, he say, I don't need the down beat. I say, that's the trouble with you. You got a feeling you don't hear. It's there. Say how, he say -- how about the people don't understand music?

I say, well, that I cannot do nothing to change the pattern of rhythm. That's the way our rhythm is. You're supposed to (inaudible). Everything here is against the beat. American music, they give you all the big boom, boom, boom, boom, boom, but THIS music don't.

I say, one, two, three, four. And, you know, the next beat is the downbeat. Somebody might be (inaudible), but on record it would be (inaudible). They can be after (inaudible) eighth note or quarter note. So you got to be able to feel it. That's the (inaudible) about this music and the complication about this music, from the same -- the same thing that they create (inaudible) to play commercial rhythm (inaudible) to. They could never be (inaudible), because (inaudible).
You put three bongo -- three congo player and each one (inaudible) play opposite the other one. And everything you do like this and (inaudible) all together, and it's like a machine over here.
